How a product backlog supports ongoing choices

Collect different kinds of candidate work: Features, defects, experience improvements, and necessary technical work can all enter the list.

Use order to express the current judgment: Order reflects value, risk, dependencies, and evidence rather than a permanent priority label.

Add detail as work gets closer: Near-term items need clear scope and completion conditions; distant ideas can wait for more evidence.

What people often confuse

A Product Backlog orders candidate work, a Product Roadmap communicates goals and direction, and a Gantt Chart schedules selected tasks. A backlog item is not automatically a delivery commitment.

You can say this to an AI Agent

Organize these features, defects, and improvements into a product backlog. Propose an order using the product goal, user impact, risk, and evidence I provide, and explain each choice. Mark unsupported judgments as assumptions. Add the problem, scope, and acceptance conditions to near-term items while keeping distant items brief. Recommend the order without promising dates or deleting lower items.
